import pandas as pd

# List of source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/training_6.csv"
]

# Target schema columns and their types (as per target examples and description)
# Name: string
# All others: integer
target_columns = [
    'Name', 'Rank', 'Team', 'Position', 'Played', 'SnapsPlayed', 'SnapsPerGame',
    'SnapsPlayedPercentage', 'RushSnapPercentage', 'TargetSnapPercentage',
    'TouchSnapPercentage', 'IntendedTouchSnapPercentage', 'FantasyPoints',
    'FantasyPointSnapPercentage'
]

# Function to convert columns to target types
def convert_types(df):
    # 'Name' as string
    df['Name'] = df['Name'].astype(str)

    # For all other columns, convert to numeric first (to handle floats), then round and convert to int
    int_columns = [
        'Rank', 'Team', 'Position', 'Played', 'SnapsPlayed', 'SnapsPerGame',
        'SnapsPlayedPercentage', 'RushSnapPercentage', 'TargetSnapPercentage',
        'TouchSnapPercentage', 'IntendedTouchSnapPercentage', 'FantasyPoints',
        'FantasyPointSnapPercentage'
    ]

    for col in int_columns:
        # Convert to numeric, coerce errors to NaN (should not happen but safe)
        df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce')
        # Round to nearest integer
        df[col] = df[col].round()
        # Convert to integer type (Int64 to allow NaNs if any)
        df[col] = df[col].astype('Int64')

    return df

# Read all source files into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # Reorder columns to target schema order if needed
    # Source columns are: ['Rank', 'Name', 'Team', 'Position', 'Played', 'SnapsPlayed', 'SnapsPerGame',
    # 'SnapsPlayedPercentage', 'RushSnapPercentage', 'TargetSnapPercentage', 'TouchSnapPercentage',
    # 'IntendedTouchSnapPercentage', 'FantasyPoints', 'FantasyPointSnapPercentage']
    # Target columns order is: ['Name', 'Rank', 'Team', 'Position', 'Played', 'SnapsPlayed', 'SnapsPerGame',
    # 'SnapsPlayedPercentage', 'RushSnapPercentage', 'TargetSnapPercentage', 'TouchSnapPercentage',
    # 'IntendedTouchSnapPercentage', 'FantasyPoints', 'FantasyPointSnapPercentage']
    # So we need to reorder and rename columns accordingly.

    # Reorder columns to target order
    df = df[['Name', 'Rank', 'Team', 'Position', 'Played', 'SnapsPlayed', 'SnapsPerGame',
             'SnapsPlayedPercentage', 'RushSnapPercentage', 'TargetSnapPercentage',
             'TouchSnapPercentage', 'IntendedTouchSnapPercentage', 'FantasyPoints',
             'FantasyPointSnapPercentage']]

    # Convert types to match target schema
    df = convert_types(df)

    dfs.append(df)

# UNION operation: concatenate all dataframes vertically
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read all source CSV files with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/training_6.csv", index_col=0)

# Join all sources on 'Name' (primary key)
df = source0.merge(source1, on='Name', how='inner', suffixes=('', '_1'))
df = df.merge(source2, on='Name', how='inner', suffixes=('', '_2'))
df = df.merge(source3, on='Name', how='inner', suffixes=('', '_3'))
df = df.merge(source4, on='Name', how='inner', suffixes=('', '_4'))
df = df.merge(source5, on='Name', how='inner', suffixes=('', '_5'))
df = df.merge(source6, on='Name', how='inner', suffixes=('', '_6'))

# After join, columns from other tables have suffixes _1, _2, ..., _6
# We need to aggregate columns by taking min (or any consistent aggregation) for each attribute across all tables
# The target schema columns are:
# ['Name': string, 'Rank': int, 'Team': int, 'Position': int, 'Played': int, 'SnapsPlayed': int, 'SnapsPerGame': int,
#  'SnapsPlayedPercentage': int, 'RushSnapPercentage': int, 'TargetSnapPercentage': int, 'TouchSnapPercentage': int,
#  'IntendedTouchSnapPercentage': int, 'FantasyPoints': int, 'FantasyPointSnapPercentage': int]

# Prepare list of columns to aggregate (all except 'Name')
agg_columns = ['Rank', 'Team', 'Position', 'Played', 'SnapsPlayed', 'SnapsPerGame',
               'SnapsPlayedPercentage', 'RushSnapPercentage', 'TargetSnapPercentage',
               'TouchSnapPercentage', 'IntendedTouchSnapPercentage', 'FantasyPoints', 'FantasyPointSnapPercentage']

# For each column, gather all versions (original + suffixed) and take min to aggregate
agg_dict = {}
for col in agg_columns:
    cols_to_agg = [col]
    for i in range(1,7):
        suffixed_col = f"{col}_{i}"
        if suffixed_col in df.columns:
            cols_to_agg.append(suffixed_col)
    # Aggregate by min ignoring NaNs
    agg_dict[col] = df[cols_to_agg].min(axis=1)

# Construct final DataFrame with 'Name' and aggregated columns
result = pd.DataFrame({'Name': df['Name']})
for col in agg_columns:
    # Convert to int as target schema expects integer types
    # Use fillna(0) before converting to int to avoid errors if any NaNs remain
    result[col] = agg_dict[col].fillna(0).astype(int)

# Write to target CSV file
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_64/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
